summary.text: Plasma is a state of matter formed when another state, often a gas, is ionized to an appreciable degree, so it holds many charged particles.
Its charged particles make it electrically conductive and very sensitive to electromagnetic fields.
Though rarely encountered on Earth, an estimated 99.9% of all ordinary matter in the universe is plasma, and stars are almost pure balls of it.

facts.label: Everyday examples
facts.value: Neon signs and lightning are partially ionized plasmas

facts.label: Name origin
facts.value: Irving Langmuir took it by analogy with blood plasma

facts.label: Fourth state idea
facts.value: Sir William Crookes proposed it in a paper in 1879

facts.label: Technology uses
facts.value: Plasma televisions, plasma etching, and fusion energy research

items.prompt: Some particles in a lit neon sign's gas are charged while others stay neutral. What is such a state called?

options.label: A fully neutral gas
A partially ionized plasma
A solid crystal of ions
A liquid held together by electrons

items.explain: Depending on conditions, neutral particles may also be present, in which case plasma is called partially ionized, as in neon signs and lightning.

items.prompt: How could a lab turn a neutral gas into plasma?

options.label: Heat it, or subject it to a strong electromagnetic field
Cool it down until its atoms stop moving
Squeeze it until it turns liquid
Strip out every charged particle it has

items.explain: Plasma can be artificially generated, for example by heating a neutral gas or subjecting it to a strong electromagnetic field.

items.prompt: Why can't scientists say at exactly what point a heated gas becomes plasma?

options.label: It happens at one fixed temperature that is hard to measure
A heated gas never becomes plasma on Earth
The transition is not well defined and depends on context
Gas and plasma are simply the same thing

items.explain: Unlike the other phase transitions, the transition to plasma is a matter of interpretation, and whether a given degree of ionization suffices depends on the phenomenon being considered.

items.prompt: What about plasma makes it electrically conductive?

options.label: It is made of tightly bound neutral atoms
It is denser than any solid
It is always completely at rest
It contains a significant portion of charged particles

items.explain: Plasma consists of a significant portion of charged particles, and their presence makes it electrically conductive.

items.prompt: A friend says the fourth state of matter must be exotic and rare everywhere. How would you correct that?

options.label: Correct, since stars are made of other states and contain none of it
Rare on Earth, but nearly all ordinary matter in the universe is in that state
Correct, since it can only be made inside special laboratories
Wrong, since it is just as common in every room on Earth

items.explain: Plasma is the fourth state of matter and, while rarely encountered on Earth, an estimated 99.9% of ordinary matter in the universe is plasma.

items.prompt: In the 1920s, Irving Langmuir watched electrons carried from heated filaments through an ionized gas. What did it remind him of when naming it?

options.label: A river carrying sand downstream
Wind carrying sparks through the air
Blood carrying red and white corpuscles
A magnet pulling iron filings along

items.explain: Langmuir first used the term by analogy with blood plasma, since the transport of electrons reminded him of the way blood plasma carries corpuscles and germs.
